inputs.root_cause: SAL-UBL-OBL-7D0855CD163E1EFD's 'allow profile-specific validators to be registered; never claim profile conformance without the installed ruleset passing' clause had no implementation anywhere: validate() checks only one hardcoded stable-profile ruleset, with no API for a caller to register a validator for a specific customization profile (EN 16931, PEPPOL BIS, or any other). Flagged as the concrete next candidate in FF6 Event 118, following the immediately preceding tick's identifier-exposure work on the same capability.

execution_steps: 1. Designed a new module, validation/profiles.py: ProfileValidatorRegistry (an immutable, customization-ID-keyed collection of validator callables -- register() returns a NEW registry rather than mutating, matching this package's existing immutable-model convention throughout XmlNode/UblDocument) and validate_profile(document, registry) (a dispatcher looking up the registered validator for the document's own customization_id and running it, returning None when nothing matches).

2. Deliberately keyed the registry by cbc:CustomizationID, not cbc:ProfileID, and documented why in the module docstring: in real UBL deployments (EN 16931 / PEPPOL BIS being the clearest examples), CustomizationID is what selects the Schematron/validation-artefact set a document must pass; ProfileID identifies the business process (ordering, billing, ...) the document participates in, not which ruleset applies to it. No SAL fact pins this down explicitly, so this is a documented design judgment matching real-world UBL tooling convention, not a literal spec quote.

3. Designed validate_profile() to return None (not an empty/passing ValidationReport) both when nothing is registered at all and when the document declares no customization ID -- matching 'absent when not installed' precisely, and structurally ruling out 'claim conformance without the installed ruleset passing': the function has no code path that could report a pass a registered validator itself did not produce.
4. Exported ProfileValidatorRegistry, ProfileValidator, and validate_profile from validation/__init__.py and the top-level package __init__.py, matching the existing export pattern.
5. Ran ruff, mypy, and the full ubl suite before writing new tests: 556 passed, unchanged (0 regressions from the new module and exports).

6. Wrote tests/python/ubl/test_obligation_profile_validator_registry.py (11 tests): registry immutability (register() leaves the original untouched, re-registering an ID replaces it, multiple distinct IDs coexist, an empty ID is refused), scoping (a validator registered for a DIFFERENT customization ID never runs against a document declaring a different one -- the clearest proof of scoping), a failing installed ruleset reported rather than softened, and 'absent when not installed' proven three ways (nothing registered at all, document declares no customization ID, a freshly built unparsed document).
7. All 11 passed on first run. Re-ran the full UBL suite: 567 passed (556 baseline + 11 new, 0 regressions). ruff and mypy clean (26 source files).
8. Promoted SAL-UBL-OBL-7D0855CD163E1EFD fully to implemented -- this closes the last of UBL-PROFILE-001's three obligations, all closed across this tick and the immediately preceding one.
